acceptanceCriteria: Heredocs, array assignments, multi-line if blocks and process substitution targets parse and the commands inside are still judged
A heredoc body is data unless a shell receives it, then it is judged or fails closed
A pipe into an interpreter with an inline program is allowed; without one it stays blocked; a download piped into any interpreter stays blocked
diagnosis: Reproduced by running extractShellSources and analyseShell over .github/workflows/*.yml: codictator.yml and release.yml report CDX-E306, test-heavy.yml reports a pipe into a shell, and the node heredoc in codictator.yml reports an unparseable embedded shell. Heredocs, arrays and plain if blocks parse on their own; four defects cause the failures. (1) shell-cmd.ts buildStripped handles a leading keyword (if/then/else/while/do) by joining the already-decoded words with spaces and re-parsing them, which loses quoting, so an if test holding a quoted GitHub expression with double braces re-parses as a brace group and fails; the rejoin also re-splits a quoted bash -c script, a fail-open risk. (2) shell-scan.ts handleRedirection reads the target of a less-than redirection as a plain word, so done with a redirect from a process substitution has an empty target and throws. (3) ShellParser.endCommand passes every heredoc body as an embedded script of the command, so the body of a node heredoc is judged as shell; a here-string body is never judged, so a shell fed by one is fail-open. (4) shell-deny.ts pipeStep flags every pipe into node, python and the other interpreters, with no allowance for an inline program (node -e), and the download check only fires when the download is adjacent to the interpreter. SPEC §4.7.2 was silent on all four and was fixed first in T-0045.
